newsitem.title: FRANCE: Comoros embassy denies intervention plans.
newsitem.headline: Comoros embassy denies intervention plans.

text.p: The Comoros embassy in Paris denied on Tuesday that government troops would intervene on two islands that have seceded from the Indian Ocean archipelago state and declared their desire to return to French control.

Embassy spokesman Mohamed Wadaane told journalists the national government on Grand Comoro, the largest of the three islands, wanted to negotiate peacefully with the separatists to create a more decentralised administration.
"The Comoran army has no plan to intervene, neither on Anjouan nor on Moheli," Wadaane said. "We favour a dialogue."
Secessionists on Anjouan island say government troops landed there on Saturday, but French journalists there have found no evidence of an intervention.
Anjouan and Moheli islands have left the federation, accusing the central government of favouring Grand Comoro.
The Comoros, with a population of 670,000, won their independence from Paris in 1975 but a fourth island in the archipelago, Mayotte, voted to remain French.
Wadaane admitted the federal system set up at independence had failed and that the local economy was in crisis.
The Comoros must now decentralise, allow the other islands to elect their own governors and have more control over their own finances, he said.
"The authorities are ready to listen to the opposition's proposals," Wadaane said, stressing the government sought a pragmatic solution to the crisis.
"It is essential that the legitimacy of the president is not questioned," he added.
President Mohamed Taki announced a plan for more island autonomy earlier this month, but secessionist leaders said it did not go far enough.
